instructions:
# Paprika: guide for agents

Document = flat map of nodes + rootIds (top-level screens/frames, in canvas coordinates).
Types: frame (container with style and layout), group (groups without painting), page (separate canvas), rect, ellipse,
text, image, path (vector with bezier curves), shape (diagram shape with text inside), connector (line/arrow between
nodes). Only frame, group and page have children.

Common fields: name, x, y, width, height (number | "hug" | "fill"), rotation, opacity (0..1),
visible, locked, layoutPositioning ("auto"|"absolute", omit = auto), constraints {horizontal: left|right|center|scale, vertical: top|bottom|center|scale} (omit = left/top; applied to non-flow children when the parent frame's numeric width or height changes), fill (color), stroke {color, width: n | "$token"}, radius (n | "$token", or on frame, rect and image [tl, tr, br, bl] with each corner n | "$token"), shadow (one object or a list of up to 8: {x, y, blur, spread: n | "$token", color, inner?}), outline {color, width: n | "$token", style?: solid|dashed|dotted, offset?}, filter and backdropFilter {blur?: n | "$token", saturate? 0..10, grayscale? 0..1, brightness? 0..10, sepia? 0..1, invert? 0..1, hueRotate? -360..360}, notes, lintIgnore (rule names lint_design skips on this node).
frame: clip (bool), layout {mode: none|row|column, gap (n | "$token"), padding (one number, [vertical, horizontal] or [top, right, bottom, left], as in CSS; each n | "$token"), align: start|center|end|stretch,
  justify: start|center|end|between, wrap}, scaledMock (true: a scaled mock, lint_design skips small-text inside it), mode (theme mode, see below). With row/column layout, children's x/y are ignored unless layoutPositioning is "absolute" (the child keeps x/y relative to the parent and is skipped by flow, gap and hug). Omit it or set "auto" to stay in the flow.
text: text, color, fontFamily (string | "$token"), fontSize (n | "$token"), fontWeight (100..900 | "$token"), lineHeight (n | "$token"; a unitless multiplier of fontSize, e.g. 1.4, never pixels: a 22px line on 16px text is 1.375), letterSpacing (n | "$token"), textAlign.
  runs (optional, up to 200): ranges {start, end} in UTF-16 indexes, sorted, not overlapping; each needs one of fontWeight (100..900 | "$token"), color, fontSize (n | "$token"), italic: true, href (http(s), mailto, or a path starting with / or #). create_nodes and update_nodes carry runs; null clears them.
  Without width/height a new text hugs its content ("hug" on both axes); give width to wrap lines.
image: src (https://, data:image/ or $asset), fit (cover|contain|fill), alt, decorative (true skips the missing-alt lint and exports alt="" aria-hidden). $asset names live on the document via set_assets.
frame and text may set href (relative, #hash, http(s), mailto, tel), exported as <a>. A root frame may set minWidth and maxWidth; export then uses width 100% between those bounds. The canvas keeps the design width.
convert_to_path turns rect and ellipse into a path with the same id (radius baked into d).
To cut a hole or merge parts, use combine_paths (operations chains union/subtract/intersect/exclude steps in one call, as names the intermediates, style picks the fill or gradient the result keeps) instead of painting the background color over the shape.
create_shape_path draws a star, polygon, ring, arc or sector from parameters (x, y = center; angles in degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock; cornerRadius rounds the corners) as an ordinary path; round_path_corners rounds the corners of a polygonal d (or a path node). Prefer them to computing vertices, arcs or fillets by hand.
group: name, x, y, opacity, visible, locked, notes, children. The box (x, y, width, height) is computed from the
  children at the end of each write; children's coordinates are relative to the group. Use group_nodes/ungroup_nodes. wrap_nodes puts the same siblings in a new frame (the drawing stays put, one undo). align_nodes (edge: left|center|right|top|middle|bottom) and distribute_nodes (axis: horizontal|vertical, at least 3) move them in one undo. show_all and unlock_all reveal hidden or locked nodes; pageId limits that to one page, and omitting it covers the whole document.
page: name, fill (canvas background), mode, notes, children. Top level only; once there are pages, every top-level node
  is a page and frames go in parentId = the page id (canvas coordinates). create_page creates the first one and, when the document already has content, moves
  that content to "Page 1" (on an empty document only the new page is created). create_page {ensure: true, name} returns the existing page of that name instead of creating another. Screens of another page: get_document_outline {rootId: page id}.
Components: a frame with component: true is a component (create_component). It may declare props (text, boolean,
  variant) and frames or groups inside it may name a slot. An instance is a frame with instanceOf = the component id,
  an optional scale, propValues and slots (create_instance). Instances may sit inside a component; a cycle is rejected.
  Children are generated copies, with derived ids and sourceId = the source id or the path slot/id or instance/copy.
  Changing the component changes every instance. On a copy, update only changes fill, color, text, src, alt, visible,
  opacity and runs (stored as an override; null goes back to the component). A nested copy is addressed by the path
  instance/copy, and that path may also carry propValues and slots. On the root, fill becomes an override and
  width/height/layout/stroke/radius/shadow/clip come from the component (use scale). A text prop drives text and
  shape text through bind.text; a boolean drives bind.visible; bind.variant omits the node unless every pair matches.
  A bind is checked when the transaction ends, so one create_nodes can carry the bound children and component: true on their frame together (or one update_nodes can set component and the binds).
  Copies cannot be moved, deleted or given children: edit the component or detach_instance.
path: d (SVG path data: M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute or relative), fill (no fill = outline only),
  stroke {color,width}, fillRule (nonzero|evenodd), strokeCap (butt|round|square), strokeJoin (miter|round|bevel),
  optional viewBox [x,y,w,h]. Without viewBox, d's coordinates are px from the node's (x,y) corner; with viewBox,
  the drawing is scaled to fit width×height (good for icons on a 24×24 grid). Without width/height, the node
  gets the drawing's box. Curves: "C c1x c1y c2x c2y x y" (cubic), "Q cx cy x y" (quadratic), S/T mirror the
  previous control point (smooth curves). Use get_bounds (absolute boxes + rotated corners) and path_info (bounds plus anchors) before positioning. edit_path moves one anchor or its handles; the index is path_info.anchors index, in the same d coordinates.
shape: shape (rect|ellipse|diamond|triangle|cylinder|parallelogram|cloud|note), text (centered; top-left on a note), color, fontFamily (string | "$token"), fontSize (n | "$token"), fontWeight (100..900 | "$token"),
  lineHeight (n | "$token"), textAlign. width/height are numbers (default 160×80; note 160×160). fill/stroke/radius/shadow paint the
  outline; fields left out on create get the kind's defaults (white with a dark border; note = yellow sticky note).
connector: from/to = {nodeId, side?: auto|top|right|bottom|left} (attached to a node) or {x, y} (free point in the
  parent's coordinates), route (straight|elbow|rounded|curve), radius (rounded corners), control {x,y} (curve handle in parent coords), startArrow/endArrow (none|arrow), stroke {color,width}, dashed,
  label (text halfway along the route, in the stroke color: "yes", "no").
  x, y, width, height and d are computed from the ends at every write (read-only): moving a shape redraws its
  connectors, and deleting a node deletes the connectors attached to it.
Diagrams: draw_diagram takes nodes (shapes) + edges (connectors) and lays out the shapes without x/y for you. Elbow and rounded arrows route around other shapes with the same parent; straight and curve do not. relayout: true with existing shape ids recomputes those routes (and applies x/y when given) in one undo step.

Colors: #hex, rgb(), rgba() or "$token" (see set_tokens); a CSS gradient or url() in fill/color is refused: use gradient {type: linear|radial|conic, angle, stops: [{color, offset}]}. On text, the glyph color is color; fill paints the text box behind it. Prefer tokens for recurring colors and sizes. set_tokens takes an optional type (color, length, fontFamily, fontWeight, fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing) and a collection name. A typed token is checked when it is set and when a node uses it; a token with no type stays a string or number and still fits any length field. A typed fontWeight or lineHeight is unitless in CSS variables; other numeric tokens stay px. detach_tokens replaces "$name" on a node with the literal resolved in that node's theme mode.
Theme modes: set_tokens with mode ("dark", "compact"…) writes only the tokens that change; a mode value must match the token's type. "mode" on a frame or page applies the mode to its subtree (the same screen can sit light and dark side by side). A collection is a name on the token, not a second value map. export_code with cssVariables: true writes var(--token) and one rule per mode.
width/height take a number, "hug" or "fill" (never a "$token"). "fill" in width/height takes the remaining space on the main axis of a parent with layout, or stretches on the cross axis.

Placement: a new top-level frame leaves x and y unset (or passes place:"free") and lands in free space, to the right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrapping to a new row past 2400px from the content's left. place is "free" | "below" | "right" | {near, side: left|right|above|below} | "none" (exact x/y). Inside a row/column frame, place:"none" with x and/or y on create_nodes, import_html or import_image sets layoutPositioning:"absolute" on each new root (unless you pass layoutPositioning) and warns, so x/y are kept instead of joining the flow. Concurrent writers never share a spot. get_document_outline and get_bounds with no ids report the content box (the union of the page's children, on any page) and the next free spot. Draw overlays (modals, menus, toasts) last, or bring them to the front with index:"front". A write warns when a new top-level node overlaps another and names the nearest free spot.

Pins: the human can point at a node or an area of the canvas and write what to do there ("Point for the AI"). Call list_pins first when the human mentions pins, and whenever a write result carries openPins; claim_pin before working on one, reply_pin to add to the thread, resolve_pin with a short reply when done (that reply is stored as an agent message on replies). wait_for_pins waits for new ones.

Recommended flow:
1. get_document_outline to get your bearings (cheap).
2. set_tokens with the palette and the type scale (pass type and collection when the token is typed). propose_tokens reads CSS variables, a Tailwind theme or JSON tokens from content you pass (the file text, never a filesystem path) and returns set_tokens operations; it does not write.
3. create_nodes with nested trees (children) in one call; prefer frames with layout over absolute positioning.
4. lint_design and fix whatever comes back as error/warning. rootIds (or rootId) lints only those subtrees. groups folds each rule to a count and the first maxIds node ids (default 8), ordered by severity; issues still lists every finding. minSeverity (info|warning|error) drops quieter findings. minFontSize raises the small-text floor (default 12). A frame with scaledMock, or lintIgnore on a node, keeps intentional small type and literal colors out of the list.
5. render_screenshot to check visually (to read a position or size, pass region + grid for a zoomed crop with coordinates in frame units instead of guessing from the image); export_image for PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF/PDF (and SVG) (raster formats use the same renderer as the screenshot); export_code to take it to code.
To bring in a ready icon or a piece of a page, use import_svg (paths, text and <use>/<symbol> sprites become editable nodes) or import_html (inline styles, or computed:true so the server renders the HTML in Chromium and inlines computed styles), import_image for a PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or GIF file (.fig and PDF are refused); export_code with format "svg" returns vector SVG.
To trace over a reference, place_reference {frameId, src, opacity?} puts it as a locked, half-transparent image at the back of the frame (compare_reference leaves it out of the render when you pass its node id as reference). When you redraw a reference image (logo, icon, UI), call analyze_image first instead of guessing coordinates by eye: it returns the palette, the background, the blobs largest first with the best-fitting primitive as a node ready for create_nodes (circle, ellipse with rotation, rect with radius, regular polygon, or a freeform outline), and layout hints (grids, repeated shapes, radial repeats). Pass frame {width,height} to get coordinates in the target frame. For an organic shape (a wing, a monogram, a whale) call trace_image to start from editable paths with the real contours (cubic beziers, holes with evenodd, sharp corners kept), then refine them; after drawing the structure, call fit_to_reference {rootId, ids, reference} to tune the numbers of the nodes you drew (position, size, rotation, radius, path anchors: you are good at structure and bad at exact numbers), then call compare_reference {rootId, reference} and fix what it reports: the global alignment first when it is significant, then the largest missing regions, then the nodes it lists as off the reference, until pass is true. render_screenshot compare is only the side-by-side picture. Do not trust rawPixelMatch: the background dominates it; act on iou.
Every write is atomic (all or nothing) and can be undone with undo. To make several calls one undo step (e.g. "draw proposal 3"), pass the same batch to each of them; the batch closes when anyone else writes or undoes in between.
Results: JSON tools also return structuredContent that matches their outputSchema; read it instead of parsing the text.
Workspaces: the server holds several documents (list_workspaces). Document tools take an optional workspaceId and read or write that workspace without open_workspace and without moving the human's canvas; omit workspaceId to use the active workspace. The outline's first line and every write result include that workspace's id and name. Undo and redo take the same workspaceId and revert only that workspace; each workspace keeps its own history for the life of the process. Edits to the workspace the canvas is showing arrive live; edits to another workspace do not switch the canvas. open_workspace still switches the active workspace for everyone, so ask the human first; create_workspace makes an empty one, rename_workspace renames one, set_workspace_cover puts an image (or a screenshot of a frame) on its card; archive_workspace hides one from list_workspaces without deleting it (the active one hands over to the most recently updated other workspace that is not archived; the only one cannot be archived) and unarchive_workspace brings it back; opening an archived workspace unarchives it; list_workspaces omits archived workspaces unless includeArchived is true, and each workspace reports archived; delete_workspace cannot be undone and takes two calls: the first, without confirmToken, returns a summary of what would be lost and a short-lived token; show that summary to the human and only call again with the token after they agree. list_workspace_ops reads who created, renamed, opened, archived, unarchived or deleted a workspace, and a delete entry keeps its summary.
The human sees your edits live on the canvas. Unknown fields are rejected with an error: read the message and adjust.

tools.name: get_design_guide
tools.title: Format guide
tools.description: Explains the node model, the accepted fields and the recommended flow. Read it before the first edit. language: "pt-BR" returns the Brazilian Portuguese version.

tools.name: get_document_outline
tools.title: Document outline
tools.description: Compact tree (one line per node: type#id, name, size, position, key style), tokens, theme modes, version and the active canvas renderer (wasm, dom, or none when no tab is connected; one value per connected tab). The first line names the workspace id and name. The last lines are the page content box and the next free spot. Cheap in tokens.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: get_nodes
tools.title: Read nodes
tools.description: Full JSON of the requested nodes (every field, with defaults). The text result is the array; structuredContent is { nodes } plus, when some ids do not exist (e.g. after an undo), `missing: [ids]` with the nodes that do exist still returned. It fails only when none of the ids exist.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: get_bounds
tools.title: Resolved geometry
tools.description: Absolute boxes for nodes after auto-layout (row/column, hug/fill, wrap), with transform origin and the four corners after rotation. Optional `ids` filters the result and lays out the page of every id, so ids on different pages all get a box; an id that exists but has no box (a page, or a node hidden inside an auto-layout frame) comes back in `unplaced`. Optional `rootId` limits to that subtree (still resolves ancestors for flex). Without both, returns every node on the first page (pass a page id as `rootId` for another page). With no ids, also returns the page content box and the next free spot.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

unplaced.description: Ids that exist but have no box: a page (no geometry) or a node hidden inside an auto-layout frame. Present only when ids is given and some of them have no box.

content.description: Page content box. Present when ids is omitted.

next.description: Top-left of the next free spot. Present when ids is omitted.

tools.name: find_nodes
tools.title: Find nodes
tools.description: Search by type, or by a substring of the name or the text, optionally inside a subtree.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

tools.name: path_info
tools.title: Path geometry
tools.description: Validates SVG path data (d) and returns the exact box of the drawing (including the extremes of bezier curves and arcs), the drawing `origin` (offset from the node origin to the path bounds), the number of segments, d normalized to absolute commands, and `anchors` (each point in path order: flat index, subpath, index within the subpath, x/y, and in/out handles when the point is curved). Pass `d` or the `id` of a path node; with `id` also returns canvasBounds, transformOrigin and rotated corners. The anchor index is what edit_path takes, in the same d coordinates.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

canvasBounds.description: With id: the box in canvas coordinates

origin.description: Offset from the node origin (0,0) to the drawing's top-left (use normalize:true on create to clear it)

transformOrigin.description: With id: CSS transform-origin (box centre) in canvas coordinates

corners.description: With id: the four corners after rotation (TL, TR, BR, BL)

anchors.description: Every anchor in path order. index is the flat index edit_path takes; at is the index inside subpath sub. in/out are omitted on a corner.

tools.name: edit_path
tools.title: Edit path point
tools.description: Moves one anchor of a path node, or its bezier handles, with the same geometry the canvas uses. index is the flat 0-based anchor from path_info.anchors (subpath 0, then subpath 1). position is in the current d coordinate space (the same numbers path_info.anchors report). If both are set, the anchor moves first (its handles translate with it) and then the handle overrides apply in that new space. handles.mirror reflects the opposite handle when only one side is set. At least one of position or handles is required. One undo step. Refuses an unknown id, a node that is not a path, a locked node, a copy inside an instance, an index past the last anchor, and an invalid d. Without viewBox the drawing shifts back to the node origin; x/y move with the box only when the node is positioned like the canvas (absolute, or not in a row/column frame). Inside a row or column frame only d, width and height change. With viewBox only d changes.

index.description: Flat 0-based anchor index, the same index path_info.anchors returns

position.description: New anchor position in the current d coordinate space

handles.description: Handle overrides applied after the anchor move. mirror reflects the opposite handle when only one of in/out is set.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

props.description: Fields written on the path node

anchors.description: Anchors after the edit, same shape as path_info.anchors

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: create_nodes
tools.title: Create nodes
tools.description: Creates one or more nodes (with nested children in frames) under parentId (null/omitted = canvas). Atomic. Returns {ids, roots, created, version}: ids is every new id (the previous created list); roots is each new node whose parent was not created in this call, as {id, name, type, x, y, width, height}; created is every new node as {id, name, type, parentId}. The text is that JSON plus one readable line per root. On a connector, x, y, width, height and d follow from/to: if a copied node carries them, create_nodes ignores those fields and says so in warnings. On a path, `normalize: true` moves the drawing to (0,0) and adds the previous offset to x/y so the node box matches the ink. place puts each root: "free" (default for a top-level node with no x/y, to the right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrapping past 2400px), "below", "right", {near, side}, or "none" for the exact x/y (inside a row/column frame the root also gets layoutPositioning "absolute", with a warning, unless you set layoutPositioning).

index.description: Position among the siblings; default: at the end

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

place.description: Where new roots go. "free" (default for a top-level node with no x/y: right of the page content, same top, gap 80, wrap past 2400px) | "below" | "right" | {near, side: left|right|above|below} | "none" (exact x/y).

openPins.description: open pins the human left in this workspace (only when there are some): call list_pins, then claim_pin and resolve_pin

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.name: update_nodes
tools.title: Update nodes
tools.description: Changes fields of several nodes in one atomic transaction. null removes a field. Objects (layout, stroke, shadow, outline, filter, backdropFilter) are replaced whole. shadow is one object or a list of up to 8. The pseudo-field index (a number, 0 = the back, or "front", "back", "forward", "backward") reorders the node in its current parent — same call, same undo step.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

workspaceId.description: Workspace to read or write. Omit it to use the active workspace (the human's canvas). Does not switch the canvas.

workspaceId.description: Workspace this write applied to

tools.title: Delete nodes
tools.description: Deletes nodes and their subtrees. Atomic, and undo brings them back. Returns {deleted, version}: every id removed, including subtrees and the connectors attached to them.

tools.title: Move nodes
tools.description: Changes the parent and/or the order of nodes (parentId null = canvas). Does not change x/y. index is the position in the new parent (0 = the back) or a step: "front", "back", "forward", "backward".

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

tools.name: group_nodes
tools.title: Group nodes
tools.description: Puts sibling nodes (same parent, no row/column layout) in a new group, in the place of the topmost one. The drawing does not move: the group's box follows its children. Returns the group id.

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

tools.name: combine_paths
tools.title: Boolean path combine
tools.description: Combines 2+ path, rect, ellipse or shape siblings into one path via union, subtract, intersect or exclude. One call can run a whole sequence: operations is a list of steps, and a step's `as` name can be used in the ids of later steps (ring = union body parts, then subtract the hole). The result keeps the bottom-most source's style unless style says otherwise (first, last, bottom, top, or {from, fill, gradient, ...}). Deletes the sources, one undo step. Use ids + operation for a single step, or operations for several, not both. An error names the failing step. Returns the new path id. Canvas UI for this is separate.

ids.description: Sibling node ids and/or `as` names of earlier steps. subtract: the first id minus the others

as.description: Name this step's result so later steps can use it in ids (it must not be an existing node id)

operations.description: A sequence of steps run in order; the last step's result is the final path. Replaces ids + operation

from.description: Id of the node to copy the style from (default: the bottom-most source)

style.description: Which source the result's style comes from: bottom (default, lowest z-order), top, first or last (in order of appearance in ids / operations), or {from: id, fill?, gradient?, stroke?, opacity?, shadow?, outline?, filter?, backdropFilter?} to copy from one node and override fields. Setting fill without gradient drops the copied gradient

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

tools.name: round_path_corners
tools.title: Round path corners
tools.description: Rounds the corners of a polygonal path (M L H V Z; curves are refused) with circular arcs, so you do not compute fillets by hand. Pass `d` (pure: returns the new d, nothing is written) or the `id` of a path node (updates its d in place, one undo step; the node box and x/y stay as they are). `radius` rounds every vertex; `radii` is one radius per vertex in the order written (a closing point equal to the start is not counted; subpaths continue the count; null or missing = `radius`, 0 = keep sharp). Each radius is clamped so the arc takes at most half of each adjacent edge. Open polylines keep both ends sharp. Returns {d, bounds} (plus id, created, version when writing).

batch.description: Undo batch: consecutive writes from this agent with the same batch become one undo step (and one history entry, labeled with the batch)

tools.name: create_shape_path
tools.title: Create shape path
tools.description: Creates one path node from a parametric shape, so you write parameters instead of coordinates. kind: star {points, radius, innerRadius? (default radius/2), angle?, cornerRadius?}; polygon {sides, radius, angle?, cornerRadius?}; ring {radius, thickness | innerRadius} (one path with a hole, fillRule evenodd); arc {radius, thickness | innerRadius, startAngle, endAngle, roundCaps?} (a band of an annulus); sector {radius, startAngle, endAngle} (a wedge from the center). tools.name: analyze_image
tools.title: Analyze reference image
tools.description: Measures a reference image so you do not have to eyeball it: call it BEFORE redrawing a logo, icon or UI from a picture, then build from the numbers. Returns the size, the background color (from the borders), a palette of dominant colors (perceptual k-means in OKLab, anti-aliasing removed) and the blobs: connected regions of one palette color, largest first (draw them in that order; nested shapes land on top). Each blob has its bbox, centroid, area, number of holes, orientation, elongation, mirror symmetry (mirrorX is left-right, mirrorY top-bottom, 1 = identical) and fit: the best primitive among circle, ellipse (with rotation), rect and roundRect (with corner radius), regular polygon (sides, rotation) or freeform, with its IoU against the blob and a node ready for create_nodes (ellipse, rect or path with fill). A blob that no primitive reaches 0.9 IoU on is freeform: it carries a Douglas-Peucker outline (up to maxPoints) and a path node; nearest names the closest primitive. A blob with holes is fitted on its silhouette (holesFilled): the holes appear as their own blobs when they have another color. layout lists repeated shapes (same color and fit within tolerance), grids (rows, cols, pitch, gap: use align_nodes/distribute_nodes or compute positions) and radial repeats (center, radius, step angle: duplicate_nodes around it). Pass frame {width,height} to get coordinates in the target frame's space (the image is fitted and centered like place_reference); without it, coordinates are source pixels. region zooms into a rectangle. Results are deterministic and the text content is a compact summary of the same data. Pure Go, no Chromium; about 50 ms for 1200x900. Reads only; the image comes from src or from an image node (nodeId). Check the result with render_screenshot compare after drawing.

tools.name: compare_reference
tools.title: Compare with reference
tools.description: Scores a drawing against its reference image, with numbers, so you know what to fix next. Call it after drawing from a reference (analyze_image, place_reference, import_image) and repeat until pass is true. It renders rootId with the same Chromium path as render_screenshot and fits the reference to that frame exactly like place_reference (centered, aspect kept). Scores ignore the background: each image is reduced to its ink (the pixels that differ from its own background; a transparent PNG counts by alpha), so a big empty background cannot inflate them. iou is ink intersection over union (the number to act on, compared with target, default 0.9; pass = iou >= target); missing is the share of the reference's ink the drawing does not cover; extra is the share of the drawn ink that is not in the reference. color gives deltaE (OKLab x100) between the dominant colors of both with their shares, pixelDeltaE over the pixels both paint (it catches swapped colors) and the drawn colors with no counterpart. rawPixelMatch is plain pixel equality, context only and misleading: the background dominates, so it reads 85-97% for drawings whose iou is 40-70%. regions lists the biggest missing and extra areas as boxes in frame coordinates with their share of the frame and color (fix the largest missing ones first). nodes lists the painting nodes under rootId whose painted pixels fall off the reference, worst first, with onReference and a suggestedMove {dx,dy} when shifting that node would land it on the reference. alignment is the best global shift (dx,dy in frame units), scale (around origin, the frame center) and with rotation: true also an angle, with iouBefore and iouAfter: when significant is true, move or scale the whole drawing in one step before fixing details. diff is a PNG (missing red, blue extra, gray matched) kept like a screenshot: url is /api/screenshot/<id>; path also writes it under the screenshot directory; includeDiff adds the image bytes inline. The last scores of each (workspace, rootId) are remembered in memory: previous and delta (current minus previous) say whether the round improved, and sameReference is false when the reference changed. Deterministic. The text content is a compact summary. reference may be the id of an image node (for instance the layer place_reference put in the frame): that node is left out of the render. Chromium is needed, as for render_screenshot.

tools.name: fit_to_reference
tools.title: Fit nodes to reference
tools.description: Tunes the numbers of nodes you already drew so the frame matches its reference image. Draw the structure first (which shapes, in what order, with what colors: you are good at that), then call this, then compare_reference: you are bad at exact numbers, this is not. It optimizes the chosen params of ids (nodes under rootId: rect, ellipse, path and frame) to maximize the ink IoU of the frame against the reference (same ink masks as compare_reference; colors are left as they are). params picks what may move: position, size, rotation (degrees, kept in -180..180), radius (rect and frame corners) and pathPoints (anchors of a path, with their handles; only the maxAnchors, default 8, with the largest local error move; paths with a viewBox are not edited). Default: position and size. Nodes in a row/column layout keep their position (the layout decides it; layoutPositioning absolute frees it), and a hug or fill size is not tuned; locked, hidden, text and other node types are skipped with a reason. How it works: the frame is rendered with Chromium once as it is and once with the tuned nodes left out; the tuned nodes are rasterized in software (rects, rounded rects, ellipses, paths with fill rule, strokes, rotation and group or frame offsets) onto the compare_reference mask, and a coordinate descent with a shrinking step (nodes with the most error first) moves the numbers, so no screenshot is taken per try. Numbers are snapped to whole or half units when that costs nothing. The result is written as one update_nodes transaction (one undo step; batch is honored; label names it) unless dryRun, and it is only written when the Chromium render of the new numbers is not worse than before. Returns per node the changes (before and after) and the anchors moved, iou.mask and iou.chromium (before and after; a gap over 0.03 is reported in warnings: text, shadows, gradients and overlapping paint are not modeled, trust the Chromium number), applied, pass (Chromium iou after >= target, default 0.99; the search stops there), iterations (rounds), and the time. About 20 nodes with the default params take under 5 s. Deterministic. Chromium is needed, as for render_screenshot. reference is a data URL, raw base64, a local path under PAPRIKA_IMPORT_DIRS or the id of an image node (left out of the render), as in compare_reference.

tools.name: trace_image
tools.title: Trace image into paths
tools.description: Turns a reference image into editable vector paths, so you do not rebuild every contour by hand (a bird's jagged wing, a monogram, a whale): trace_image first, then refine the paths. Segments the image into palette-color blobs (the same ones analyze_image reports) and creates ONE path node per blob, fill = the blob color, largest silhouette first so nested shapes land on top. The outer contour and the holes are subpaths of the same path with fillRule evenodd; contours are cubic bezier chains: corners (turning angle >= smoothness) stay sharp, the rest is fitted to within tolerance px. A hole that another traced blob fills is closed (the blob on top covers it, no seam); a hole that shows the background stays open. Coordinates are in parentId's space: the image is fitted inside the frame and centered, like place_reference and analyze_image's frame; each node box matches its ink (normalize: true). The background color is not drawn unless includeBackground (set the frame's fill to background.color). Creates the nodes the way create_nodes does (one undo step, batch honoured) and returns ids/roots/created plus per-path stats (points, segments, curves, lines, corners, error), the total node count, and truncated when more than maxPaths blobs were found. dryRun: true returns each path's d and the stats without writing. Deterministic, pure Go, no Chromium. Photos and gradients give many noisy blobs: lower maxColors, raise minArea or pass colors. Check the result with render_screenshot compare.

tools.name: duplicate_nodes
tools.title: Duplicate nodes
tools.description: Duplicates nodes with their whole subtree in one undo step (new ids; instances stay instances of the same component, scale multiplies their scale; connectors between duplicated nodes point at the copies, the others keep their ends). Each copy goes in its source's parent. With no offset, place defaults to the right of the source (gap 80) so the copy does not land on it; place is "free" | "below" | "right" | {near, side} | "none" ("below" and "right" sit beside the source, gap 80, like {near: source, side}; "free" goes past the page content), and an explicit offset nudges x and y. scale grows or shrinks the copy from its own top-left corner: sizes, children positions, text size, strokes, radius, shadow, gap and padding; hug/fill stay. props is written on each copy's root (for example {mode: "dark"} for a light/dark pair). Returns copies (one id per source) and map (every source node to its copy), plus ids, roots and created in the same shape as create_nodes. The text is that JSON plus one readable line per root.
